evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: A00906-001 她 entry; historical variant account
evidence.text: The entry identifies 她 as a historical variant of 姐. It quotes the Jiyun listing 姐 alongside 她 and 媎, and reports the old mother-related gloss for 姐. It distinguishes the later feminine third-person use, read tā. Its accompanying 姐 entry analyzes 姐 as 女 plus 且; this does not place 也 in modern 姐.
evidence.title: [A00906] 姐 - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.field: A00906-001 她 entry; quoted Six Books of the Late Han and Jiyun accounts
evidence.text: The entry quotes the Jiyun account listing 她 as an alternative old spelling of 姐, and quotes 說文解字 for 姐’s mother-related regional gloss and 女 plus 且 analysis. It does not report 也 as a phonetic element of modern 她; the 也-as-sound claim belongs to a separately reported account of an old 姐 spelling.

search_audit.query: 她 姐 古文 六書故 也聲 異體 字典
search_audit.outcome: Inspected the Ministry of Education character-variant entry. It separates the old spelling 她 as a variant of 姐 from the later pronoun use. Search results also surfaced a secondary report that 六書故 describes an old 姐 spelling with 也 as phonetic; that reported construction is not evidence that modern 姐 contains 也.

gaps: The exact earliest witness and date of 她 as an old spelling of 姐 remain unverified; the inspected Ministry entry reports later dictionary evidence, not an early artifact.

The claim that 也 served as a phonetic element is a reported analysis of an old alternative 姐 spelling. The inspected primary-style dictionary entry does not independently establish its historical sound correspondence, nor does it establish 也 as a sound component of modern 她.

The official Unicode character lookups for 她 and 也 were inaccessible. Local readings supplied with the packet are not external click-through evidence; modern Mandarin readings alone do not prove an ancient sound relation.
No early 她 glyph image was established. The selected image is a modern redraw of 也 and can illustrate only the graph named in the reported sound analysis, not the historical form of 她 or 姐.
